sections.html:
The Josephine County seat, Grants Pass lies on Interstate 5 beside the Rogue River in the Rogue Valley of southern Oregon, northwest of Medford. It stands at about 960 feet and covers roughly 11 square miles. Josephine County is big at 1,642 square miles and had 88,090 residents in the 2020 Census.

Most of the county is public land: the Forest Service owns about 39 percent and the Bureau of Land Management about 28 percent. That is why so many homes back up to national forest and not farmland, and why access, wells and fire risk come up in sales.

The city's 2020 population was 39,189, up from 34,533 in 2010. It has 16,681 housing units and 15,865 households, and 54.9 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The median age is 41.3, and 23.3 percent of residents are 65 or older, so inherited and downsizing sales are common.

sections.h2: Hot summers, wet winters and wildfire
sections.html:
Summers are hot and dry and winters are mild and wetter. About 31 inches of precipitation falls in a year, with roughly three quarters of it between November 1 and March 31. August highs average 90.6 degrees, and the city sees about 51 afternoons a year at or above 90 degrees and 8 at or above 100. The record high is 115 degrees, set on July 4, 2022. Snow is light.

Smoke and fire risk come with living in southwest Oregon. In July 2025 the Board Shanty Fire grew to 409 acres south of Grants Pass and triggered Level 2 evacuation notices in several Josephine County zones. A property near forest land may have higher insurance costs or fewer insurers, so gather your current policy and any fire-mitigation work before you list.

sections.h2: Roads, schools and what buyers weigh
sections.html:
Interstate 5 runs through the area, and U.S. Route 199 passes through the city and joins I-5. The Redwood Highway heads south toward California. Freeway access helps with commuters to the Medford area, while a rural property on a private road faces a different set of questions.

The Grants Pass School District serves the city, including Grants Pass High School, and Three Rivers School District covers other parts of the county. Rogue Community College's Redwood Campus is just south of the city. As with any Oregon sale, confirm the district for your address before you describe it.

sections.h2: Local economy and what it means for demand
sections.html:
Lumber was the major employer until the early 1970s. Automation and federal timber cuts then drove a long decline, and at least 20 mills in the region closed after 1980. Today the work is more varied: outdoor recreation with guided Rogue River fishing and boat trips, health care, and small and medium businesses. Dutch Bros coffee was founded in Grants Pass in 1992.

A mixed economy means buyers include retirees, remote workers and local families. Riverside Park, the Cathedral Hills Trail System and the Rogue River are the sort of nearby features buyers ask about, so mention whichever ones are close to your house.

sections.h2: Rural properties: wells, septic and private roads
sections.html:
With so much wooded and rural land around town, plenty of sellers own homes on wells, septic systems or private roads, and buyers and lenders ask about each. Pull together service records, any well test, septic pumping or inspection receipts, and a road maintenance agreement if neighbors share the cost.

Documented answers keep a deal moving. A property with gaps in its paperwork tends to draw a lower offer than one where the owner can show what was done and when. If a private road has no written agreement, say so, because a buyer's lender may ask who maintains it.

Sections 14.800 to 14.840 of the Grants Pass development code govern vacation rental dwellings. A Director-issued permit and a Title 4 license are required before a unit is advertised, and only single-family dwellings and existing accessory dwelling units qualify.

  • Stays are limited to 27 days in any 30-day period.
  • Overnight occupancy is two people per sleeping room plus two more, capped at 12.
  • Parking is two cars in the driveway and one on the street.
  • The transient room tax applies, and a guest register must be kept.

If you inherited a house that has been run as a vacation rental, confirm the permit status before you list. A buyer relying on rental income will want to see that the permit and license are in order.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates in Josephine County
sections.html:
Statements are mailed across Oregon by October 25. Pay once or in installments.

Payment optionDue dateDiscount
Full amountNovember 153 percent
Two-thirdsNovember 152 percent
InstallmentsNovember 15, February 15, May 15Interest if paid late

Late payments accrue interest at 1.333 percent per month.

If you sell mid-year, title will show anything unpaid along with the split for the current year, and escrow settles the balance out of your proceeds. Asking for that payoff number in advance keeps closing day calm.

Under ORS 105.464, each buyer who makes a written offer on covered residential property receives a disclosure statement from the seller. The form covers water, sewage, structure, systems, flooding, settling and other known defects.

Buyers can revoke within five days unless they gave up that right. An exclusion is available to court-appointed personal representatives, trustees and conservators, and to banks selling after foreclosure. For a house on a well or septic, note what you know about their condition.

sections.h2: What Grants Pass sellers usually face
sections.html:
• Heirs handling a parent's house from another state.
  • Homes on wells, septic systems or private roads that need documentation.
  • Properties near forest land where fire risk affects insurance.
  • Landlords with aging rentals and vacation rental permit questions.
  • Owners facing short timelines after a job loss.

sections.h2: Selling for cash in Grants Pass
sections.html:
A cash buyer brings no lender and no appraisal, which lets you skip repairs and showings and choose your own closing date. A title company records the deed with the county and pays off any mortgage or unpaid tax out of your proceeds.

That does not make the deal automatic. Compare the written offer with what a listing would cost you in repairs, commissions and months of holding the house. We buy houses in Grants Pass in their current condition, and you can request an offer online or by phone.

Having the right papers on hand speeds things up. Gather your latest tax statement, a mortgage payoff figure, the well and septic records, and any rental permit. An out-of-state heir can sign remotely through the title company, so you do not have to travel for the closing. Tell the title officer early where each signer lives, and the paperwork can be arranged to match.

faqs.q: What is the population of Grants Pass?
faqs.a: The 2020 Census counted 39,189 people, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 39,239.

faqs.q: Why do so many Grants Pass homes sit near public land?
faqs.a: Most of Josephine County is federal land, with the Forest Service owning about 39 percent and the Bureau of Land Management about 28 percent. Fire risk and road access are common questions for those homes.

faqs.q: When is the first Oregon property tax installment due?
faqs.a: November 15. The remaining installments are due February 15 and May 15.

faqs.q: Can I run a vacation rental from a Grants Pass house?
faqs.a: Yes, but only with a city permit and license, and stays are limited to 27 days in a 30-day period.

faqs.q: How long do I have to revoke an offer on a Grants Pass house?
faqs.a: A buyer has five days after receiving the seller's disclosure statement to revoke, unless the buyer waived that right.
